name: Greenbriar Apartments (scattered site)
headline: CARE Communities won 2026 federal 4% credits to renovate Greenbriar, its first apartment community (40 units, built 1994-95 at 400-434 Butch Cassidy Drive in north Fort Collins), with all 40 homes kept affordable at 60% AMI.
why_it_matters: Greenbriar's original 1993 tax credit carried only a 30-year commitment, so this recapitalization is what keeps the 40 homes affordable. It also fixes failing sewer and plumbing lines. It shows how CARE re-paired its properties (first with Windtrail, now with Fairbrooke) to fit the bond and gap money available.

status.label: Credits awarded; renovation planned for 2027
status.detail: CHFA lists the award (amounts 'subject to change'). CARE told residents that renovations at Greenbriar and Fairbrooke begin in 2027. No public record of a financing closing or permits yet.

next_step: Watch for the Housing Catalyst bond issue and closing on the combined Greenbriar-Fairbrooke financing, and for the City funding agreement for the $1.5M award.

key_numbers.meaning: Every unit is income-restricted at 60% AMI: 20 two-bedrooms and 20 three-bedrooms.
About $8.9M over 10 years, roughly $22,200 per unit per year. The site is in a Qualified Census Tract.

key_numbers.value: $5,600,000 in private activity bonds (Housing Catalyst issuer)
key_numbers.meaning: About $140,000 of bonds per unit. Whose cap backs it is not stated.

key_numbers.value: $1.5M city gap award, shared with Fairbrooke
key_numbers.meaning: Fort Collins fully funded CARE's combined 76-unit Greenbriar-Fairbrooke rehab in June 2026.

background.text: Greenbriar was CARE Housing's first community: 40 units in 10 buildings, built new in 1994-95 with a 1993 CHFA 9% award ($153,534, plus a $95,708 supplemental in 1995). The original commitment was 30 years, so the original compliance term has largely run (inferred from the dates).

In March 2024 CARE asked the City for $10,812,010 of 2024 bond cap to rehab Greenbriar and Windtrail (90 units) under one tax credit partnership, with Housing Catalyst or CHFA as issuer. It also asked Larimer County for $6.5M. Windtrail later went ahead alone (2025 CHFA 4% award, $9M bonds), and Greenbriar is now paired with Fairbrooke Heights.

Main physical problem: the exterior sewer line from the buildings to the city main has been damaged by shifting ground and tree roots, causing backups into apartments. CARE plans new sewer and unit plumbing lines throughout, work under the parking lot, and repaving.

Planned unit work (2026 FAQ): new appliances, countertops and cabinets, plumbing fixtures, flooring, washers and dryers, central air conditioning, new windows and lighting. Depending on budget, a renovated clubhouse, expanded garden, seating areas, landscaping, trash enclosures and sidewalk and pavement repairs. The 2024 plan also named Enterprise Green Communities and Energy Star targets, covered bike storage and community Wi-Fi.
Residents will be moved temporarily (on site, to another CARE community or to a hotel) for about 6-8 weeks, with at least 30 days' notice. CARE pays approved moving costs.

City gap funding: the combined $1.5M Greenbriar-Fairbrooke request was ranked last of 7 by the Affordable Housing Board but #3 by the Human Services and Housing Funding Board. It was fully funded under Resolution 2026-078, adopted 16 June 2026.

Bond cap context: the City's 2026 cap went to Country Ranch and Bristlecone (Resolution 2026-077). The City's 2025 cap ($11,184,752) went to Housing Catalyst for Windtrail 'and elsewhere in the City' (Resolution 2025-066), which Housing Catalyst may carry forward for up to 3 years.
Before the rehab, a January 2024 market-study inventory showed Greenbriar Village with 9 units at 50% AMI and 31 at 60%, with rents below the maximums. Post-rehab, CHFA shows all 40 at 60%.

2026 CHFA maximum gross rents at 60% AMI in Larimer County: $1,761 for a two-bedroom and $2,034 for a three-bedroom. CARE describes Greenbriar as 2- and 3-bedroom apartments, which matches CHFA's 20/20 split. Actual rents are not public.

discrepancies.text: Address: CHFA's 2026 award report gives 400 Butch Cassidy Drive; CARE's 2024 bond application and CHFA's 1993 status report give 400-434 Butch Cassidy Drive (same property).
Pairing: CARE's 2024 bond request paired Greenbriar with Windtrail, while the 2026 City award and the CARE FAQ pair it with Fairbrooke Heights.
